text.p: A simple Senate resolution supporting the troops after the U.S. cruise missile strikes against Iraq stumbled on presidential politics on Thursday, two months before Election Day.
The main problem is that Republicans and Democrats cannot agree on giving credit to President Bill Clinton for the action.
"The Democrats would like for us to endorse Clinton's reelection ... all his foreign policy, all his defence failures. We don't want to do that," Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott told reporters.
Indiana Republican Richard Lugar said the Democrats had proposed a "very laudatory campaign statement."

"In large measure, it appears that there are some Republicans who are reluctant to be a part of providing any real praise for the president," said Democratic Leader Tom Daschle. "I think that's unfortunate."

Daschle proposed that the Senate pass a bipartisan resolution on Tuesday after the first of two missile attacks was launched against Iraqi targets. Late on Thursday senators from the two parties were still negotiating the text.
The issue is complicated by Republican complaints that the Clinton administration dropped the ball on earlier policy towards Iraq, making the strikes necessary.
They said they wanted to know more about where the policy was headed.
"Republicans are not too sure of what there is to commend in this process," said Lugar. He said Lott was keeping in touch with Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole on the issue.
Lugar also said there were "sizeable" disagreements among Republicans on what the resolution should say.
Sen. Kay Bailey Hutchison, R-Texas, said Democrats were being "unreasonable" in wanting to commend Clinton when he had not set out his objectives and had failed to consult Congress.
But both Lott and Daschle predicted that eventually agreement would be reached on language the Senate could approve.
